part.text: The test confirms the expected behavior: with the default `maxBodyLength: -1`, requests through `follow-redirects` should be unlimited. The bug is in `applyFollowRedirectsBodyLimit` (lib/adapters/http.js:2980) — it only sets `options.maxBodyLength` when the value is positive, so `follow-redirects` falls back to its own 10MB default. When `maxRedirects === 0`, plain `http` is used and no limit applies, hence the inconsistency.

part.text:
Done. The fix is in lib/adapters/http.js (`applyFollowRedirectsBodyLimit`):

```js
options.maxBodyLength = maxBodyLength > -1 ? maxBodyLength : Infinity;
```

Previously, when `config.maxBodyLength` was the default `-1` (unlimited), the option wasn't passed to `follow-redirects`, which then silently enforced its own 10MB default — while `maxRedirects: 0` (plain `http`) had no limit. Now the unlimited default is consistently forwarded as `Infinity`, and explicit positive limits are still honored.

Validation: the failing test `should properly support default max body length (follow-redirects as well)` now passes; the full unit suite went from 62 passing / 4 failing (baseline) to 63 passing / 3 failing — the remaining 3 failures are pre-existing environment issues unrelated to this change.
